items.title: 1. Opening with pressure
items.quote: 1. Opening with pressure. First come, first serve. Last unit. Last price. You haven't asked him anything and you're already squeezing.

items.title: 2. Asking nothing but budget
items.quote: 2. Asking nothing but budget. He gives you a number, you tell him it's too low and he needs to pay more. You learned one thing about him and used it against him - he will never opens up.

items.title: 3. Pushing an offer below what you just said the owner would take
items.quote: 3. Pushing an offer below what you just said the owner would take. Usually because you're reviving the deal the previous client walked away from. People aren't stupid. They know when they're solving someone else's problem.

items.title: 4. Ignoring everything except the money
items.quote: 4. Ignoring everything except the money. He tells you size, layout, who's living there, what he's already rejected. You send whatever fits the budget line. With your budget you can only get this. The clients know - you are pushing your STOCK. People want to be heard. When your manager said open your ears and close your mouth, that's what he meant.

items.title: 5. Not knowing your numbers
items.quote: 5. Not knowing your numbers. Square footage. Price per square foot. His currency. Go vague and he decides you don't know your own stock. He'll make this decision once or twice in his life. He won't hand it to someone guessing. None of this makes you dishonest - but most of the times your are Getting ghosted just because of that.
